text:
morgan: Heads up — noticed long-running chat sessions show steady RSS growth even after requests finish. heap snapshots look like a ton of tiny free holes in the KV cache allocator rather than large live allocations. anyone else seen this?

riley: yup saw similar on canary last week. hole density goes up with context length. suspect allocator fragmentation + our slab sizes not matching token chunking.

anya: do you have a quick diff of the profile? can you paste the allocation histogram?

morgan: pasted a short snippet from pprof (heap alloc buckets):

```
0-256B: 3.2M
256-1kB: 6.1M
1k-4kB: 1.1M
4kB+: 120k
free-holes-estimate: ~42% of slab space
avg-slot-util: 0.47
evicted-bytes/sec during tail: 1.1MB
```

samir: that free-holes-estimate is the killer. Our block size defaults to 4KB slablets with buddy-like suballoc. Small tokens end up wasting 50-75% of each subblock.

riley: two quick levers: increase minimal allocation unit or add an opportunistic compaction pass during idle cycles. But compaction pauses may impact tail latency.

anya: what about adaptive packing: if we detect high hole density and low allocation churn, run a background relinker that coalesces adjacent live segments into denser slabs. no global stop-the-world.

morgan: sketch of what I tested locally: trigger when hole_density > 0.35 and avg_slot_util < 0.6 for 30s. compaction threads take one slab at a time, try to copy live KV into new slab allocation, update bucket pointers via atomic compare-and-swap. fallback if CAS fails.

```
// pseudo
if (hole_density > 0.35 && util < 0.6 && idle_window >= 30s) {
  spawn background_compactor(one_slab_id);
}
```

riley: nice. did you measure pause/latency impact?

morgan: yes — background copying kept p99 token generation unchanged. single-slab compaction had transient memory bump (~8-12%) while copying but freed ~24% after completes. steady-state RSS improved after a few compactions.

samir: how did you pick slab candidates? earliest-last-touch or highest-hole-ratio?

morgan: highest-hole-ratio first; also prefer slabs with low live-count to reduce copy-work. that minimized intermediate memory overhead in my run.

anya: two concerns: 1) frequent compaction can thrash write-path if we don't rate-limit; 2) we need safe pointer swap for concurrent reads without global locks. CAS-based pointer swap + versioned slab header should be fine but needs rigorous fuzzing.

riley: alternative is tuning block granularity: increase suballoc bucket sizes for long-context workloads. e.g., move from 4B/16B/64B lanes to 8B/32B/128B — fewer small fragments. downside: wasted space for workloads with many tiny caches.

samir: could be a dynamic profile-guided policy — on load start, sample token size distribution for a minute and pick bucket sizes. combined with background compaction for historic churn.

morgan: I'll open a small RFC with two proposals: (A) adaptive_bucket_sizing + sampling, (B) opportunistic single-slab compactor with CAS pointer-swap. include perf numbers from my local canary (attached). Want volunteers to review fuzz tests and latency runbook.

anya: +1 to reviewing. I can take the compaction correctness fuzzing and help write the CAS smoke tests.

riley: I'll prototype dynamic bucket sampler and run microbench for token distributions.

samir: I'll add a guardrail in the runtime to cap background compaction memory growth and throttle copy rate per-GPU thread. also add telemetry: compaction_runs, average_copy_bytes, pre/post hole_density.
